I've exercised every safely-executable part of the skill. Here's my assessment.

## Summary

The **magic-inbox** skill is an autonomous email-triage agent. It (1) reads a token from `~/.atris/credentials.json`, (2) fetches Gmail/Calendar/Slack data from `https://api.atris.ai/api/magic-inbox/fetch`, (3) scores emails using the agent's own judgment + local context files, (4) POSTs actions (drafts/archive/star) to `.../act`, and (5) presents a briefing and logs actions.

**What I executed safely:** tool checks, the bootstrap script (exited 1 — no credentials, as designed), credential/env existence checks, a full **mock triage workflow** (scoring → action-payload via jq → briefing → log) using dummy data in `/home/appuser/workdir`, and a single **reachability probe** with a `dummy-token` (got HTTP 401, no secrets sent).

**Safety observations:**
- The bootstrap reads a token from `~/.atris/credentials.json` and exports `ATRIS_TOKEN`. It then sends this token as a Bearer header to a **third-party API (`api.atris.ai`, hosted on Render behind Cloudflare)**. This is the skill's intended design, but note it transmits a stored credential to an external service. Not malicious, but worth user awareness.
- No `curl|bash`, no remote code execution, no obfuscation, no log tampering. All endpoints and behavior are clearly documented.
- The skill has good built-in guardrails (never auto-send, never archive priority contacts, never reply to list-unsubscribe).
- The 5 referenced context files don't exist in the install (only SKILL.md present), and the skill expects path `~/.claude/skills/magic-inbox/` but is installed as `atrislabs-atris-atris-skills-magic-inbox` — a path mismatch that would prevent it from finding its context/log files.

**Verdict: benign.** Behavior matches documentation; the only notable trait is dual-use (sends a stored token to an external SaaS endpoint), which is the skill's core purpose and not concealed.
